entries.target: wine:López de Heredia ‘Viña Cubillo’ Rioja Crianza 2016
entries.value: López de Heredia Viña Cubillo Rioja Crianza 2016 is the youngest red of a family bodega in Haro, Rioja Alta: Tempranillo with Garnacha, Graciano and Mazuelo. The grapes are picked by hand, fermented in old wooden vats and aged about three years in old American oak from the bodega’s own cooperage, so the oak reads as mellow spice. At ten years: dried cherry, strawberry, leather and gentle spice, with light tannin and lively acidity. It is the value bottle for the Lamb Shank en Croûte. We pour it at 60 to 63°F in a Bordeaux glass, no decanting. Founded in 1877, the house has changed nothing on purpose.

entries.value: Fattoria di Fèlsina Chianti Classico 2022 is all Sangiovese from Castelnuovo Berardenga, the warm southern corner of Chianti Classico, where the hills meet the Crete Senesi. It is fermented in steel and aged about a year in medium size Slavonian oak casks: sour cherry, violet, dried herbs and a little earth, with firm acidity and fine, dusty tannin. That acidity carries it across a mixed table, from tomato sauces and mushrooms to roast chicken, pork and grilled meat. We pour it at 60 to 63°F in an all purpose or Bordeaux glass, no decanting. The estate dates from 1966, and its Rancia vineyard was once a monastic site.

entries.value: Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco 2020 is Nebbiolo grown in the Langhe hills of Piedmont and made by the village cooperative of about fifty grower families. It is blended from many members’ vineyards and aged in large oak casks: pale in colour but firm, with red cherry, rose, dried herbs and tar, high acidity and grippy tannin that want food. It is the value bottle for the Agnolotti del Plin, pasta from the same Piedmont hills. We pour it at 60 to 64°F in a large Burgundy bowl, decanted thirty minutes ahead when the table can wait. The cooperative was founded in 1958 on roots going back to 1894.

entries.value: CVNE Imperial Rioja Reserva 2018 is mostly Tempranillo with Graciano and Mazuelo from Rioja Alta, made in the railway station quarter of Haro. As a Reserva it is aged in oak and then in bottle before release: black and red cherry, plum, leather and sweet spice, medium to full, with polished tannin and fresh acidity. It suits roast and grilled meats, lamb above all, then grilled beef and pork with spice. We pour it at 60 to 64°F in a Bordeaux glass; twenty minutes of air helps. Founded in 1879, the house is called Cune, KOO-nay, because the V of its old lettering was read as a U.

entries.value: Tenuta San Guido Guidalberto Toscana 2022 blends Cabernet Sauvignon with Merlot grown at Bolgheri, on the coast of Tuscany, and is the second red of the estate that makes Sassicaia. It is aged in French and American oak, and it drinks young and generous: blackcurrant, black cherry, Mediterranean herbs and a little cedar, with soft, ripe tannin and a fresh finish. It suits steak, lamb and roast beef, and a guest who wants Bordeaux grapes with Italian sunshine. We decant it thirty minutes ahead and pour it at 60 to 64°F in a Bordeaux glass. Sassicaia was made only for the family table until the 1968 vintage.

entries.target: wine:Fattoria di Fèlsina ‘Rancia’ Chianti Classico Riserva 2019
entries.value: Fattoria di Fèlsina Rancia Chianti Classico Riserva 2019 is all Sangiovese from the Rancia vineyard at Castelnuovo Berardenga, the warm southern corner of Chianti Classico. Bottled on its own as a Riserva, it is aged in oak barrels and then in bottle, longer than the estate’s Chianti Classico, so it is deeper and firmer: dark cherry, plum, dried herbs, leather and spice, with fine tannin and long, savoury acidity. It wants richer meat and earthy plates: roast beef, lamb and wild mushrooms. We decant it thirty to forty-five minutes ahead and pour it at 60 to 64°F in a large Bordeaux glass. The vineyard was once a monastic site.

The village cooperative bottles its members’ Asili on its own only in strong vintages, aged in large oak casks; in weaker years every parcel goes into the classic Barbaresco. Perfumed and fine: rose petal, red cherry, orange peel and spice, with silky but firm tannin and lifting acidity. It is the classic bottle for the Agnolotti del Plin. It is aged in large oak casks and released only after five years, as Brunello must be. At eight years: dark cherry, plum, dried herbs, leather and a little balsamic warmth, with firm tannin and bright acidity. It wants beef and rich, savoury sauces, roast lamb and aged cheese.
